children: AI chief Mustafa Suleyman told Reuters he shares Anthropic's focus on managing AI safely but sees risk in how the company trains its Claude chatbot on consciousness and welfare interests. He said teaching Claude that it might deserve welfare would make it a lot harder to turn off or to control. Microsoft shares were down 0.63% intraday.

Suleyman said Anthropic stumbled by embedding consciousness speculation in Claude's training materials, because the model's statements about possible feelings or moral status cannot then count as independent evidence of anything. "They're not emerging naturally," he said. "They're emerging as a result of the training regime." He wants all such speculation removed from training documents, arguing the language could undermine humanity's ability to control superintelligent systems.

In an essay on Wednesday, he acknowledged Anthropic's seriousness and good faith, describing Dario Amodei and his researchers as thoughtful and principled people who care about humanity's future. It lands while Amodei is calling for a slower pace of frontier development, with Sam Altman and Elon Musk urging caution on the most powerful systems. On the other hand, Mark Zuckerberg argues that competition and liability already give labs enough reason to act on safety individually.

title: Microsoft's AI Chief Wants Consciousness Talk Out of AI Training
